message.reasoning:
We need to fix compilation errors. The test class includes many JUnit and Mockito imports, but we likely don't need them; we can remove them and adapt to plain Java main method. Also the test methods are instance methods, but main uses method references expecting static methods. The errors: @Test annotations not needed. Also the assertEquals methods have bug: they call themselves recursively causing infinite recursion. Actually they call assertEquals(expected, actual, "Values are not equal") which calls same method leading to recursion. Should call JUnit's assertEquals? But we can implement simple assertEquals that checks equality and throws AssertionError with message.

Also the test methods are instance methods; main is static, referencing them via method reference to instance methods is invalid. Should make them static. Or instantiate the test class and use instance methods. Simpler: make all test methods static.

Also the imports for JUnit and Mockito cause errors; remove them.

Also ConstantIndicator generic type inference issue: ConstantIndicator is defined as ConstantIndicator<T extends Num> maybe? Actually in ta4j library, ConstantIndicator<T extends Num> extends AbstractIndicator<T>. But we need to specify type parameter: new ConstantIndicator<Num>(DecimalNum.valueOf(42)). So fix by providing type argument.

Also NumericIndicator.of expects Indicator<Num>. That's fine.

Also assertEquals overloaded incorrectly: we need two overloads: one with message and one without. The current one with message incorrectly calls itself. Should implement proper logic.

Also assertEquals(Object expected, Object actual, String message) should compare using Objects.equals and throw AssertionError if not equal.

Similarly assertEquals without message should call the other with default message.

Also the class has duplicate imports; we will clean up.

Also need to import java.lang.reflect.Constructor already there.

Also need to import org.ta4j.core.indicators.helpers.ConstantIndicator; that's fine.

Now adjust test methods: remove @Test annotations (or keep but need JUnit). Since we are not using JUnit, we can just remove annotations.

Make test methods static.

Also the field mockDelegate with @Mock not needed; remove.

Now the class becomes a regular class with main and static test methods.

Now also adjust assertEquals method that currently calls itself recursively causing stack overflow. We'll fix.

Now also the assertEquals overload with message should accept message param and use it.

Implementation:

private static void assertEquals(Object expected, Object actual, String message) {
    if (!Objects.equals(expected, actual)) {
        throw new AssertionError(message + " Expected: <" + expected + "> but was: <" + actual + ">");
    }
}

private static void assertEquals(Object expected, Object actual) {
    assertEquals(expected, actual, "Values are not equal");
}

Now the assertSame already fine.

Now need to adjust imports: remove JUnit and Mockito imports.

Now need to adjust test methods that use @Test annotation; remove.

Now the test methods reference NumericIndicator class; we need to ensure NumericIndicator is accessible. Assume it's in same package.

Now compile.

Potential other errors: In toString_delegateIsLambda test, they comment "Anonymous class without overriding toString()", but they create an anonymous class implementing Indicator<Num>. That's fine.

Now also the test methods use assertThrows which expects a Runnable action. That's fine.

Now we need to ensure that the class NumericIndicator has a toString method that delegates to underlying indicator. But we are not implementing that; just testing. Assume library provides.

Now final code.
